models_evaluated: Inpatient prognosis at admission model (supervised machine learning mortality prediction)

links.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) of clinicians alone, model alone, and clinicians combined with model
links.effect: Model AUC 0.834 vs clinicians 0.753 (p<0.0001); integrating clinician predictions with model raised AUC to 0.853 (p<0.0001).
links.quote: Integrating clinician predictions with the model's estimates further increased the AUC to 0.853 (p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: Model versus clinician estimates on discrimination, calibration, and net benefit on same admissions
links.effect: Model outperformed clinicians (AUC 0.834 vs 0.753, p<0.0001); clinicians overestimated risk while the model was extremely well-calibrated; model showed net benefit across thresholds.
links.quote: The model performed better than the clinician estimates (AUC 0.834 vs. 0.753, p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: Prospective performance of the model on live admissions before EHR implementation
links.effect: Prospective analysis of 1,069 admissions; model AUC 0.834 and extremely well calibrated; subsequently implemented in the EMR.
links.quote: This study is a prospective analysis of 1,069 solid tumor medical oncology hospital admissions (n = 911 unique patients) from February 7 to June 7, 2022, at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center.

screen.reason: Prospective comparative study evaluating a machine learning mortality risk model against clinician estimates and testing the combination/integration of clinician predictions with model estimates.

primary.practice: integrating clinician judgment with machine learning predictions
